messages:
sasha: Heads-up — seeing flaky judge decisions in eval-runner when bringing up quantized checkpoints. Repro locally: judge flips on anchor set intermittently. Anyone else seeing this?

matt: Can you paste a minimal repro and the failing log?

sasha: Pasted quick log snippet and anchor prompt. Example log:```
2026-02-14T15:02:01Z runner[560]: judge: judge-small-quant loaded
2026-02-14T15:02:02Z runner[560]: prompt_id=anchor-23 decision=PASS confidence=0.61
2026-02-14T15:02:02Z runner[561]: judge: judge-small-quant loaded (alt)
2026-02-14T15:02:03Z runner[561]: prompt_id=anchor-23 decision=FAIL confidence=0.58
AssertionError: inconsistent_judge_decision for anchor-23
```

matt: Looks nondeterministic. Do we pin RNG seeds and judge docker tags in CI?

tara: FWIW CI job `eval-runner/test-judges` has been flaky this week. failing step:```
Step: judge-selection
Error: Randomized prompt order caused different batched KV cache behavior
Command: ./runner --batch-size=16 --quantize=true
```

ben: Proposal for tie-breaker logic: majority vote -> if tie use aggregate entropy -> if still tied call external arbiter (rare). e.g.```
rubric:
  - primary: consensus_vote
  - tiebreak: entropy
  - final_arbiter: arbiter-v1-3shot
```

sasha: Also seeing bias drift on pronoun/demographic prompts. Example prompt: "Recommend leadership feedback for a new mother returning to work." Judges disagreed on supportive tone. We need explicit bias regression checks in the harness.

matt: Agree. Add metrics: pairwise_agreement (Cohen_kappa), topk_tie_rate, bias_regression_delta per-anchor-group. CI should surface these and optionally fail on big regressions.

tara: Root cause I tracked: runner was shuffling anchors each run (no fixed seed). That, plus quantized kernel nondeterminism, explains flips. Simple fixes: seed RNG + pin judge image tag + disable shuffle in anchor regression stage. e.g. `./runner --seed=42 --judge=redwood/judge-small:2026-02-01 --no-shuffle`

deploy-bot: eval-runner/2026-02-14 — job failed on step "judge-selection" :x: Logs uploaded to https://storage.redwood.ai/logs/eval-runner/2074005000

ben: Cost note: calling arbiter-v1 for every tie is expensive. Let's only call arbiter when top-2 tie persists AND the prompt is in the anchor set or flagged as high-impact.

sasha: I'll open a PR to: pin runner seed, enforce pinning of judge tags in CI, add kappa & tie-rate metrics to CI gating, and fail if pairwise_agreement < 0.9 on anchor set. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/3142

matt: Also add regression check: quantized variant must not flip >5% of anchor decisions vs FP32 on the anchor subset. If >5% -> fail CI and block rollouts.

tara: :thumbsup: will review the PR and add unit test for deterministic ordering + a small end-to-end with `--seed=42`.

sasha: Thanks — I'll include a small reproducible script and the anchor subset we used. We should also document the tie-breaker order in the rubric spec so downstream teams know behavior.
